relationships.subject: oxaliplatin
relationships.evidence_quote: Our results show that oxaliplatin exposure induced a statistically significant and time-dependent increase of VEGF-A that was blunted by the inhibitor of glial cell metabolism fluorocitrate

relationships.subject: VEGF-A
relationships.evidence_quote: Treatment with either oxaliplatin or VEGF165b caused a statistically significant increase in SP and CGRP release compared to control slices (Fig. 9).

relationships.subject: VEGFR-1
relationships.evidence_quote: The co-treatment with D16F7, but not with DC101, reversed the increase in SP and CGRP release induced by oxaliplatin or VEGF165b (Fig. 9), indicating that the pain-related signaling is mediated by VEGFR-1.

relationships.subject: VEGF-A
relationships.evidence_quote: Treatment with either oxaliplatin or VEGF165b for 6 ​h reduced more than 50 ​% the expression of EAAT1 and EAAT2 genes compared to the control group (Fig. 10).

relationships.subject: VEGFR-2
relationships.evidence_quote: Taken together, these results confirmed that VEGF-A also plays a neuroprotective role, mediated by the VEGFR-2 receptor.

key_findings: VEGF-A has a dual role in oxaliplatin neurotoxicity: pain-related signaling (SP/CGRP release, EAAT1/2 reduction) via VEGFR-1 and neuroprotection via VEGFR-2.
Oxaliplatin induced astrocyte-derived VEGF-A release in spinal cord slices; selective VEGFR-1 blockade is suggested as a strategy.
